transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I suppose... things have just been feeling kind of flat lately. Heavy, I guess. 

The stuff I normally do—like going on photography walks, or mentoring the kids... even just keeping my calendar straight for work—I just... I stopped doing them. I haven't really been initiating anything right now. That's mostly why I'm here.
Did something specific happen in your life before this started?

I don't know... it's been a while. Maybe a year and three months? Give or take. 

My, um... a family member got sick around then. Their behavior changed a lot, too. I had to step in, coordinate everything for them. That's when this started, I guess.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Yeah, I guess so. Like I said before... the photography, mentoring... it just doesn't feel the same. It's all just... flat. I don't really want to do any of it anymore.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I don't know if I'd call it depressed. I'm not really... sad, or anything like that. Just... what I said before. Flat.
Have these changes been tied to any specific stressful event or life change?

I mean... like I just said a minute ago. It's been about a year and three months. It started right after my family member got sick and their behavior changed. I had to take on coordinating everything for them. So... yeah. That's when it started.
Have you been feeling depressed or down most days, nearly every day?
I... I think you just asked me that. Like I said, I wouldn't call it depressed. Just... flat. That's all.
Have you been diagnosed with a medical or neurological illness around the time this began?
No. I haven't been diagnosed with anything like that.
Has this flat or low feeling been present most days for at least two years?
No. I just told you... it started about a year and three months ago. When my family member got sick. Not two years.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling sad or down most of the day nearly every day?
I... I don't think so. I mean, I wouldn't say sad. Just... like I said before. Flat.
Did these symptoms begin within a few months after your family member got sick and you had to take on those responsibilities?
Yeah. Like I said... it's been about a year and three months. It started right after their health and behavior changed, and I had to take on all the coordination for them. So... yes. Around then.
Have these feelings and changes been making it hard for you to function at work, at home, or in your relationships?

Work is... mostly fine. It's intact. I guess I've missed a few calendar details here and there... I've had to double-check tasks that used to just be automatic for me. 

As for the rest... I've pulled back from things. Like my photography outings, and mentoring. I just... I don't feel as present. Or reliable, I guess.
Do these changes feel distressing to you?
I... I don't know if I'd use that word. It's just... how things are right now. I haven't really thought much about how I feel about it.
Have these changes been causing you significant distress?
I think I just... I wouldn't really use that word. I'm not in distress. It's just... dealing with how things are right now. I haven't really dwelled on it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Sleep is... it's been different, I suppose. There are nights where I'll only get maybe two or three hours. I'll just wake up way before dawn. But I don't feel tired. I just... get up and feel ready to start answering emails or organizing the appointment lists for the day. It just is what it is.
Over the past few weeks, would you say you’ve felt depressed or down most of the day, nearly every day?
No... I wouldn't say that. I haven't really felt down. Just... going about my day.
How much distress do these changes cause you?

I mean... I wouldn't call it distress. It's just... things are a bit off. Work is mostly fine, but I've... missed a few details on the calendar lately. Had to double-check things that usually just... happen automatically for me. And outside of work, I just haven't felt like doing much. I haven't gone out for photography in a while, and I... I stepped back from mentoring. I just don't feel like I'm really... there, or reliable right now. But I wouldn't say I'm distressed.
Would you say these changes have been significantly affecting your functioning day to day?

Like I just said... not significantly, no. Work has stayed intact overall. I just... have to double-check those calendar details and tasks that used to be automatic for me. And... yeah, I've pulled back from the photography outings and the mentoring because I just don't feel as present or reliable right now. But I'm still functioning.
Have you had a period of feeling unusually euphoric, elevated, or overly energized?

I guess there are times... stretches where I feel pretty upbeat. Like everything is just clicking perfectly. But... then something small happens. Like someone moves a meeting on the schedule, and I... I get kind of sharp with people. It surprises me, honestly. But yeah, sometimes I feel really energized.
When you have those upbeat, energized periods, how long do they usually last?

I'm not exactly sure how many days each one lasts, but... they've been coming and going for about eleven months now. Just these stretches where I feel really driven. I don't sleep as much during them, and... I guess I feel a bit too confident about things. But yeah... it's been recurring for about eleven months.
During those times when you feel unusually energized and confident, have you ever needed hospital care or caused major problems because of it?
No... no hospital. I haven't caused any major problems. Just... just what I said before.
